references.text: Uses the same Hebrew word 'kapper' (atonement) in connection with the people's sin and atonement.
Explains the principle that blood provides atonement for the soul, which is the basis for the atonement ritual in Deuteronomy 21:8.
Concerns how innocent blood defiles the land and can only be atoned for by the blood of the one who shed it.
A prayer asking God to atone (kapper) for the people's sins for His name's sake, similar to the prayer in Deuteronomy 21:8.
Refers to how the Lord has redeemed (padah) Israel, using the same word for 'ransom' as in Deuteronomy 21:8.
Jeremiah declares his innocence and warns against shedding innocent blood, linking to the theme of innocent blood.
The Lord declares that He will cleanse their blood which He has not cleansed, a thematic parallel to the atonement for blood.
Explains that almost everything is cleansed with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness - fulfilling the principle of atonement.
Describes how believers are ransomed (redeemed) by Christ's precious blood, fulfilling the 'padah' (ransom) theme.
